selected.spoken: What If We Gave Mars a Thicker Atmosphere?

candidates.spoken: Above 19 kPa, people could walk outside without pressure suits.
What If We Gave Mars a Thicker Atmosphere?
Above that, people could skip pressure suits.
Today, Mars has about 1% of Earth's air pressure.
Terraforming Mars isn't just warming it.
So terraforming Mars is a problem of scale, not physics.
It would not all happen at once.
Additional volatiles must be supplied from an external source.
So once added, the air would mostly stay.
Why Mars needs air pressure above 19 kilopascals.

script.spoken: Why Mars needs air pressure above 19 kilopascals. Above that, people could skip pressure suits. Today, Mars has about 1% of Earth's air pressure. One idea: redirect asteroids carrying 40 to 400 billion tonnes of volatiles. Mars loses air only slowly, about 1 millibar per billion years. So once added, the air would mostly stay. So terraforming Mars is a problem of scale, not physics.
